mailchimpSyncSettings.mergeFieldHelp:
Determines which value is written to a Mailchimp merge field. Combine multiple expressions with | (OR) – the first match wins.

Available expressions:
• user.firstName / user.name – first or last name
• slug:contains:value – "1" if the subscription slug contains "value"
• slug:contains_any:v1,v2 – "1" if any of the values is contained
• slug:equals:value – "1" on exact match

errorHelp.raw: Original message from the mail server:

tls.cause: The mail server encrypted the connection with TLS, but its certificate is not trusted (self-signed, expired, or issued for a different hostname). The mail was not delivered.
tls.fix:
1. Check the SMTP host and port under Settings › Integrations › Mail.
2. Make sure your mail server is really the one answering there — another program often occupies the port (locally e.g. Proton Mail Bridge on port 1025).
3. Use a mail server with a valid certificate, or locally an SMTP server without TLS (e.g. Mailpit on a free port).

connectionRefused.cause: Nothing accepts connections on the configured SMTP host and port.
connectionRefused.fix:
1. Check host and port under Settings › Integrations › Mail.
2. Start the mail server (locally e.g. «docker compose up mailpit»).
3. Check whether a firewall blocks the port.

hostNotFound.cause: The mail server hostname cannot be resolved — it does not exist or DNS is unreachable.
hostNotFound.fix:
1. Check the SMTP host for typos (Settings › Integrations › Mail).
2. Inside Docker use the service name (e.g. «mailpit» instead of «localhost»).

timeout.cause: The mail server did not answer in time. Usually a firewall blocks the port or the server is overloaded.
timeout.fix:
1. Check whether the port is reachable from this server.
2. Many hosts block port 25 — use 587 or 465.
3. Try the send again later.

auth.cause: The mail provider rejected the credentials.
auth.fix:
1. Renew the API key or user and password under Settings › Integrations › Mail.
2. Check that the key belongs to the right account and region.

recipientRejected.cause: The mail server rejected the recipient address — it does not exist, or the sender domain is not allowed to send to it.
recipientRejected.fix:
1. Check the recipient address.
2. Verify the sender domain with your provider (SPF/DKIM).
3. In sandbox mode (e.g. Mailgun) recipients must be authorised first.

rateLimit.cause: The provider hit its sending limit and rejected further mails for now.
rateLimit.fix:
1. Wait and run the send again later.
2. Check the quota of your plan with the mail provider.

noProvider.cause: No mail provider is configured, so nothing can be sent.
noProvider.fix: Set up a provider under Settings › Integrations › Mail (SMTP, Mailgun, Mailchimp or Slack).

templateMissing.cause: The mail template used here no longer exists.
templateMissing.fix: Pick an existing template under «Mail templates» or create it again, then start the send once more.

generic.cause: The mail server rejected the send with the message below.
generic.fix:
1. Check the configuration under Settings › Integrations › Mail.
2. Look into the server log for the full error.
3. Send a test mail from the template to check the connection.

sync.hint: Asks the mail provider for the current delivery state of every mail that is still open.

stateHelp.legendIntro: The state shows how far a mail got on its way to the recipient. It is reported by the mail provider, not by We.Publish itself.
stateHelp.legendFooter:
State updates normally arrive from the mail provider by webhook. With no webhook configured — or on a local installation the provider cannot reach — the state stays at “submitted”. “Refresh states” then fetches it from the provider directly.
SMTP and Slack report no delivery states at all, so those mails stay at “submitted”.

submitted.name: submitted
submitted.meaning: We.Publish handed the mail to the mail provider and the provider accepted it. It is queued there. This state says nothing yet about the recipient's mailbox.
submitted.next: Wait: the provider reports the outcome later by webhook. If the state sits here for a long time, usually no webhook is configured — use “Refresh states” to fetch the current state.

accepted.name: accepted
accepted.meaning: The receiving mail server accepted the message for the recipient. Mailgun reports this intermediate step; Mandrill skips it and goes straight to “delivered”.

delivered.name: delivered
delivered.meaning: The recipient's mail server accepted the message and delivered it to the mailbox. This is the successful end state. Mandrill calls it “Delivered” in its UI and “sent” in its API.
delivered.next: Nothing. Note that delivered does not mean read — and does not rule out the mail landing in the spam folder.

deferred.name: deferred
deferred.meaning: The receiving server temporarily refused the message — greylisting, a rate limit, a full mailbox or a short outage. The provider keeps retrying automatically for hours.
deferred.next: Wait. The state moves to “delivered” or “bounced” on its own. Sending again by hand only produces a duplicate.

bounced.name: bounced
bounced.meaning: Delivery failed permanently. Hard bounce: the address or the domain does not exist. Soft bounce: repeated temporary failures (full mailbox, server permanently unreachable) that never resolved.
bounced.next: Check the recipient address for typos, then correct or remove it. Repeated hard bounces to the same address damage the sending domain's reputation. The exact SMTP reason is in the “Error” column and in the provider's log.

rejected.name: rejected
rejected.meaning: The mail was never sent. Either We.Publish could not hand it over (missing or wrong provider configuration), or the provider refused it up front: unverified sending domain (“unsigned”), address on the provider's suppression list after an earlier hard bounce or spam complaint, unsubscribed recipient, or the account's sending limit was reached.
rejected.next: The “Error” column names the reason — hover it for cause and remedy. Fix the cause and send again: nothing is retried automatically.
